title: Chapter 18. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — II: kirtana and dance (conclusion), bhavavesha, the festivals of the year, prarthanas
html:
Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 18: the end of the cycle of kirtana and dance in Navadvipa (GPT, section 4.2), two padas on the Lord's bhavas (the bhava of Balarama; the Lord in the bhava of Radha waiting for Krishna), the festivals of the year — the "twelve-month lila" (GPT, section 5.1: the swing-jhulana, Janmashtami and Nanda-utsava, Radhashtami, the remembrance of the rasa-lila, spring and Holi) and two prarthanas. Before translation the "Narahari" signatures in these sections were checked throughout in GPT1 (tesseract recognition): the catalogue had missed several more padas. The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2 and with the Bhakti-ratnakara (eds. 1912 and 1960; almost all padas of the chapter are in its 12th wave); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. Padas signed "Ghanashyama" (the same Narahari Chakravarti) are not included in the appendix. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.

1. Narahari — "kibā khola karatāla bāje…" (GPT1 p. 267, no. 61; BR)

Kirtana: the khol and karatalas sound, the associates stand around; they sing the sweet lila at which wood and stone melt; Gaura dances, and no one knows by what bhava He is seized; His body thrills, streams of tears flow from His eyes; He embraces the fallen and gives the treasure of prema to everyone — only the poet is left out. Raga nata. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); short payar with Vrajabuli forms.1

কিবা খোল করতাল বাজে ।
চারি পাশে পরিকর সাজে ॥

kibā khola karatāla bāje |
cāri pāśe parikara sāje ||

kibā khola karatāla bāje — how the khol and karatalas sound; cāri pāśe — on all four sides; parikara sāje — the associates are adorned

1.1How the khol and karatalas resound!
All around stand the adorned associates.

আজু গায়ত মধুর লীলা ।
শুনি দরবয়ে দারুশিলা ॥

āju gāyata madhura līlā |
śuni darabaye dāruśilā ||

āju gāyata — today they sing; madhura līlā — the sweet lila; śuni — hearing; darabaye — melt; dāru-śilā — wood and stone

1.2Today they sing the sweet lila —
hearing it, wood and stone melt.

রঙ্গে নাচয়ে সুন্দর গোরা ।
কেবা জানে কিবা ভাবে ভোরা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

raṅge nācaye sundara gorā |
kebā jāne kibā bhābe bhorā || dhru ||

raṅge nācaye — joyfully dances; sundara gorā — beautiful Gora; kebā jāne — who knows; kibā bhābe bhorā — by what bhava He is overwhelmed

1.3(Refrain) Joyfully the beautiful Gora dances —
who knows by what bhava He is seized?

নব পুলক-বলিত তনু ।
শোহে কনক-পনস জনু ॥

naba pulaka-balita tanu |
śohe kanaka-panasa janu ||

naba pulaka-balita tanu — the body covered with fresh thrills; śohe — shines; kanaka-panasa janu — like a golden jackfruit

1.4His body is covered with fresh thrills —
as if a golden jackfruit were shining.2

সুরসরিত-প্রবাহ পারা ।
দুটী নয়নে বহয়ে ধারা ॥

surasarita-prabāha pārā |
duṭī nayane bahaye dhārā ||

sura-sarita-prabāha pārā — like the current of the celestial river (Ganga); duṭī nayane — from both eyes; bahaye dhārā — streams flow

1.5Like the current of the celestial river,
streams flow from both His eyes.3

ঘন ঘন ভুজযুগ তুলি ।
গরজয়ে হরি হরি বলি ॥

ghana ghana bhujayuga tuli |
garajaye hari hari bali ||

ghana ghana — again and again; bhuja-yuga tuli — raising both arms; garajaye — He thunders; hari hari bali — saying "Hari, Hari"

1.6Again and again raising both arms,
He thunders: "Hari, Hari!"

অতি পতিত পামরে হেরি ।
ধরি কোরে করে বেরি বেরি ॥

ati patita pāmare heri |
dhari kore kare beri beri ||

ati patita pāmare heri — seeing the most fallen and sinful; dhari kore kare — He takes them into His embrace; beri beri — again and again

1.7Seeing the most fallen and sinful,
again and again He clasps them in His embrace.

প্রেমধন দেই জনে জনে ।
ছাড়ি একা নরহরি দীনে ॥

premadhana dei jane jane |
chāṛi ekā narahari dīne ||

prema-dhana dei — gives the treasure of prema; jane jane — to each person; chāṛi — leaving out; ekā narahari dīne — the one wretched Narahari

1.8To each and every one He gives the treasure of prema,
passing over only one wretched Narahari.4

vv. 2783–2790): Ishana, showing Srinivasa Navadvipa, quotes it at the house of Sanjaya, "dear to the Lord", where Vishvambhara danced, right after the pada "nācata śacītanaya gaura" (chapter 17, no. 27). The GPT2 index assigns the page to Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The Lord's dancing in kirtana in Navadvipa — CB Madhya 8, 23; CC Adi 17. (panasa). one passed over by the mercy given to all.

2. Narahari — "bhubanamohana gorācām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 268, no. 63; BR)

Dancing in prema: Gorachand, enchanter of the world, dances weeping, cries "Hari!", embraces the fallen, floods everyone with His rasa, throws Himself on the ground and rolls in the dust; seeing this, all living beings weep. Raga varadi or dhanashi. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave), though its language is a simple Bengali payar.5

ভুবনমোহন গোরাচাঁদ ।
অখিল লোকের মনোফাঁদ ॥

bhubanamohana gorācām̐da |
akhila lokera manophām̐da ||

bhubana-mohana — enchanter of the world; gorā-cām̐da — Gorachand (Gora the moon); akhila lokera — of all people; mano-phām̐da — the snare of hearts

2.1Gorachand, the enchanter of the world —
a net that snares the hearts of all people.6

নাচে পহু প্রেমের আবেশে ।
অরুণ-নয়ন জলে ভাসে ॥

nāce pahu premera ābeśe |
aruṇa-nayana jale bhāse ||

nāce pahu — the Lord dances; premera ābeśe — absorbed in prema; aruṇa-nayana — reddened eyes; jale bhāse — swim in tears

2.2The Lord dances, seized by prema;
His reddened eyes swim in tears.

ভুজ তুলি হরি হরি বোলে ।
পতিতে ধরিয়া করে কোলে ॥

bhuja tuli hari hari bole |
patite dhariyā kare kole ||

bhuja tuli — raising His arms; hari hari bole — cries "Hari, Hari"; patite dhariyā — seizing the fallen; kare kole — takes them to His breast

2.3Raising His arms, He cries: "Hari, Hari!" —
and, seizing the fallen, clasps them to His breast.

নিজ রসে সভায় ভাসায় ।
চারি পাশে পারিষদ গায় ॥

nija rase sabhāya bhāsāya |
cāri pāśe pāriṣada gāya ||

nija rase — with His own rasa; sabhāya bhāsāya — floods everyone; cāri pāśe — all around; pāriṣada gāya — the associates sing

2.4With His own rasa He floods everyone;
all around His associates sing.

সুকোমল অঙ্গ আছাড়িয়া ।
গড়ি যায় ধুলায় পড়িয়া ॥

sukomala aṅga āchāṛiyā |
gaṛi yāya dhulāya paṛiyā ||

sukomala aṅga — His most tender body; āchāṛiyā — flinging down; gaṛi yāya — He rolls; dhulāya paṛiyā — falling into the dust

2.5Flinging His most tender body to the ground,
He falls and rolls in the dust.

দেখিয়া সকল জীব কাঁদে ।
নরহরি হিয়া নাহি বাঁধে ॥

dekhiyā sakala jība kām̐de |
narahari hiyā nāhi bām̐dhe ||

dekhiyā — seeing this; sakala jība kām̐de — all living beings weep; narahari hiyā — Narahari's heart; nāhi bām̐dhe — cannot hold firm

2.6Seeing this, all living beings weep;
Narahari's heart finds no rest.

1960, vv. 2795–2800), at the same place, the house of Sanjaya; after the pada — "under this tree the Lord stayed a while and went on by the road to the Ganga". Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. all people". These are the readings of the second occurrence of the same pada in the BR: Narahari Chakravarti quotes it twice — at the house of Sanjaya (vv. 2795–2800) and at the house of Srivasa (ed. 1960, v. 3397 ff., "bhubanapābana gorācām̐da | akhila jībera mana-phām̐da").

3. Narahari — "nācata gaurakiśora. suradhunītīre ujora…" (GPT1 p. 268, no. 65; BR)

Dancing on the bank of the Suradhuni: young Gaura with hundreds of associates, making no distinction between His own and others, gives away the treasure of prema, weeps in a peerless bhava and, speaking in a faltering voice, takes Gadadhara by the hand. Raga dhanashi. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); short payar with Vrajabuli forms.7

নাচত গৌরকিশোর ।
সুরধুনীতীরে উজোর ॥

nācata gaurakiśora |
suradhunītīre ujora ||

nācata — dances; gaura-kiśora — young Gaura; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); ujora — shining, illumining

3.1Young Gaura dances,
illumining the bank of the Suradhuni.

কত শত পরিকর সঙ্গ ।
কীর্তনে অতুলিত অঙ্গ ॥

kata śata parikara saṅga |
kīrtane atulita aṅga ||

kata śata parikara saṅga — with Him hundreds of associates; kīrtane — in the kirtana; atulita aṅga — peerless limbs (movements)

3.2With Him are hundreds of associates;
in the kirtana His movements are peerless.8

নিজ পর কাছু না জান ।
প্রেমরতন করু দান ॥

nija para kāchu nā jāna |
premaratana karu dāna ||

nija para — own and others; kāchu nā jāna — He does not distinguish at all; prema-ratana — the jewel of prema; karu dāna — He gives away

3.3Making no distinction between His own and others,
He gives away the treasure of prema.

নিরুপম ভাবে বিভোর ।
অরুণ-নয়নে ঝরে লোর ॥

nirupama bhābe bibhora |
aruṇa-nayane jhare lora ||

nirupama bhābe — in a peerless bhava; bibhora — absorbed; aruṇa-nayane — from the reddened eyes; jhare lora — tears flow

3.4Immersed in a peerless bhava,
He sheds tears from His reddened eyes.

কহি কত গদ গদ বাণী ।
ধরই গদাধর-পাণি ॥

kahi kata gada gada bāṇī |
dharai gadādhara-pāṇi ||

kahi kata — uttering so many; gada gada bāṇī — words in a faltering voice; dharai — He takes; gadādhara-pāṇi — Gadadhara's hand

3.5Uttering so many words in a faltering voice,
He takes Gadadhara by the hand.9

ঘন ঘন কাঁপয়ে অঙ্গ ।
নরহরি কি বুঝব রঙ্গ ॥

ghana ghana kām̐paye aṅga |
narahari ki bujhaba raṅga ||

ghana ghana — again and again; kām̐paye aṅga — the body trembles; narahari — Narahari; ki bujhaba raṅga — what will he understand of this play

3.6Again and again His body trembles —
what can Narahari grasp of this play?

vv. 2889–2894): Ishana shows the bank of the Ganga where the Lord danced with His associates and quotes several padas in a row (including the next one, no. 4); after them — "having spread the good fortune of the Ganga, the Lord went home this way with His associates". Not in PK, KGC, PS. The Gita-chandrodaya (ed. 1948, no. 30) has a pada with the same opening ("heranu gaurakiśora | suradhanītīre ujora"), but it is a different song — signed by Kavishekhara Raya and with a different text after the first couplet; the common opening is probably a current formula. B. Krishna-lila. This is the prema of Vraja, not worldly attachment.

4. Narahari Dasa — "gaura suradhunītīre nācata…" (GPT1 p. 268, no. 66; BR)

Dancing on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura's body takes away the pride of a golden mountain, His locks are adorned with flowers, at the sight of His arms and breast Kama loses his peace; He walks with the gait of a king of elephants, from His lotus eyes flow as it were two Gangas, the earth rejoices at the rhythm of His feet. Raga gauri. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli with chains of assonance.10

গৌর সুরধুনীতীরে নাচত সুঘড় পরিকর সঙ্গ ।
হেম-ভূধর-গৌরব-ভর-হর পরম মধুরিম অঙ্গ ॥

gaura suradhunītīre nācata sughaṛa parikara saṅga |
hema-bhūdhara-gauraba-bhara-hara parama madhurima aṅga ||

gaura suradhunī-tīre nācata — Gaura dances on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); sughaṛa parikara saṅga — with skilful associates; hema-bhūdhara-gauraba-bhara-hara — removing the pride of a golden mountain; parama madhurima aṅga — a body of supreme sweetness

4.1Gaura dances on the bank of the Suradhuni with His skilful associates;
His body, full of supreme sweetness, takes away the pride of a golden mountain.

অতুল কুন্তল বলিত কেতকী কুন্দ কুসুম সুরঙ্গ ।
বাহু বলনি বিশাল বক্ষ বিলোকি বিকল অনঙ্গ ॥

atula kuntala balita ketakī kunda kusuma suraṅga |
bāhu balani biśāla bakṣa biloki bikala anaṅga ||

atula kuntala — peerless locks; balita ketakī kunda kusuma suraṅga — adorned with ketaki, kunda and bright flowers; bāhu balani — the curve of the arms; biśāla bakṣa — the broad chest; biloki — seeing; bikala anaṅga — Ananga (Kama) is agitated

4.2His peerless locks are adorned with ketaki, kunda jasmine and bright flowers;
seeing the curve of His arms and His broad chest, Ananga loses his peace.11

ভাবে গরগর গমন গজপতি গঞ্জি গরজে অভঙ্গ ।
কঞ্জ-লোচনে লোর ঢরকত প্রকট জনু যুগ গঙ্গ ॥

bhābe garagara gamana gajapati gañji garaje abhaṅga |
kañja-locane lora ḍharakata prakaṭa janu yuga gaṅga ||

bhābe garagara — overwhelmed by bhava; gamana gajapati gañji — with a gait that shames the king of elephants; garaje abhaṅga — He thunders unceasingly; kañja-locane — from the lotus eyes; lora ḍharakata — tears roll; prakaṭa janu yuga gaṅga — as if two Gangas appeared

4.3Seized by bhava, He steps, putting to shame the king of elephants, and thunders unceasingly; tears roll from His lotus eyes — as if two Gangas had appeared.

তরল পদতলে তাল ধরইতে ধরণী অধিক উমঙ্গ ।
দাস নরহরি করত জয় জয় কার কি কহব রঙ্গ ॥

tarala padatale tāla dharaite dharaṇī adhika umaṅga |
dāsa narahari karata jaya jaya kāra ki kahaba raṅga ||

tarala pada-tale — with the unsteady soles; tāla dharaite — as He keeps the rhythm; dharaṇī adhika umaṅga — the earth rejoices exceedingly; dāsa narahari — Narahari Dasa; karata jaya jaya kāra — cries "glory, glory"; ki kahaba raṅga — what shall I say of the play

4.4When His unsteady feet keep the rhythm, the earth rejoices beyond measure;
Narahari Dasa cries: "Glory, glory!" — what can be said of this play?

vv. 2895–2898), right after the preceding pada, at the Ganga. The GPT1 recognition of this pada is faulty; the readings are restored from GPT2 and the BR (see the full version of the book). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. and kunda are flowers.

5. Narahari Dasa — "bali-kalidamana śamanabhayabhañjana…" (GPT1 p. 269, no. 67; BR)

The son of Shachi dancing in the midst of the kirtana: subduer of Kali and of the fear of death, skilful giver of prema, more beautiful than a golden mountain; at the rhythm of His feet the earth sways, He spreads His arms, smiles, and seeing Gadadhara's face loses His composure; His eyes reveal the former play of Vraja. Raga belavali. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.12

বলি-কলিদমন শমনভয়ভঞ্জন নিখিল-ভুবন-জনরঞ্জনকারী ।
দুলহ প্রেমধন-বিতরণ-পণ্ডিত সুরতরুনিকর-গরব-ভরহারী ॥

bali-kalidamana śamanabhayabhañjana nikhila-bhubana-janarañjanakārī |
dulaha premadhana-bitaraṇa-paṇḍita suratarunikara-garaba-bharahārī ||

bali-kali-damana — subduer of mighty Kali; śamana-bhaya-bhañjana — destroyer of the fear of Yama; nikhila-bhubana-jana-rañjana-kārī — giving joy to the people of all worlds; dulaha prema-dhana-bitaraṇa-paṇḍita — skilled in distributing the rare treasure of prema; sura-taru-nikara-garaba-bhara-hārī — removing the pride of all the wish-fulfilling trees

5.1Subduer of mighty Kali, dispeller of the fear of Yama, giver of joy to the people of all the worlds, skilled in giving away the rare treasure of prema, taking away the pride of all the wish-fulfilling trees —13

নাচত শচীসুত কীর্তন মাঝ ।
কনক-ধরাধর নিন্দি রুচির তনু বিলসত জনু নব মনমথরাজ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

nācata śacīsuta kīrtana mājha |
kanaka-dharādhara nindi rucira tanu bilasata janu naba manamatharāja || dhru ||

nācata śacī-suta — the son of Shachi dances; kīrtana mājha — in the midst of the kirtana; kanaka-dharādhara nindi — surpassing a golden mountain; rucira tanu — the lovely body; bilasata — shines; janu naba manamatha-rāja — like a new king Manmatha

5.2(Refrain) the son of Shachi dances in the midst of the kirtana;
His body, lovelier than a golden mountain, shines like a new king Manmatha.

পদতল-তালে ধরণী করু টলমল ললিত ভঙ্গী ভুজ রহত পসারি ।
হাসত মৃদু মৃদু অধর কম্প অতি অথির গদাধর-বদন নেহারি ॥

padatala-tāle dharaṇī karu ṭalamala lalita bhaṅgī bhuja rahata pasāri |
hāsata mṛdu mṛdu adhara kampa ati athira gadādhara-badana nehāri ||

pada-tala-tāle — at the rhythm of the feet; dharaṇī karu ṭalamala — the earth sways; lalita bhaṅgī — gracefully bending; bhuja rahata pasāri — He keeps His arms spread; hāsata mṛdu mṛdu — smiling gently; adhara kampa ati — the lips tremble much; athira — unsteady; gadādhara-badana nehāri — on seeing Gadadhara's face

5.3At the rhythm of His feet the earth sways; gracefully bending, He spreads His arms;
smiling gently, His lips tremble — and seeing Gadadhara's face, He loses His composure.

ডগমগ নয়ন-কমল ঘন ঘূরত নিরুপম পূরব রঙ্গ পরকাশ ।
উলসিত পরম চতুর পরিকরগণ ইহ রসে বঞ্চিত নরহরি দাস ॥

ḍagamaga nayana-kamala ghana ghūrata nirupama pūraba raṅga parakāśa |
ulasita parama catura parikaragaṇa iha rase bañcita narahari dāsa ||

ḍagamaga nayana-kamala — the lotus eyes sway; ghana ghūrata — turn again and again; nirupama pūraba raṅga parakāśa — revealing the peerless former play; ulasita — rejoice; parama catura parikara-gaṇa — the most skilful associates; iha rase bañcita — deprived of this rasa; narahari dāsa — Narahari Dasa

5.4His lotus eyes sway, turning again and again, revealing the peerless former play;
the skilful associates rejoice — only Narahari Dasa is deprived of this rasa.14

vv. 3018–3021): "here Gaurachandra, with joy in His heart, danced in sankirtana in a wondrous bhava". Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. consequences. The wish-fulfilling tree (sura-taru, kalpa-vriksha) grants only what is asked for, but the Lord gives prema beyond asking. Krishna-lila (note 9).

6. Narahari — "āju gorā nagarakīrtane…" (GPT1 p. 269, no. 68; BR)

The night-time city kirtana: adorned Gora walks with His associates, dances, pours down a rain of prema; gods disguised as men shower flowers, the townspeople run and sing, fools hearing the lion's roar expect disaster; hundreds of thousands of lamps are burning, the whole world is intoxicated. Raga kamoda. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of the night kirtana); Bengali payar.15

আজু গোরা নগরকীর্তনে ।
